- ★ How to score 16+ out of 20
- ২০ নম্বরের মধ্যে ১৬+ পাওয়ার কৌশল
- Exam: 100 MCQs in 90 min, −0.25 per wrong answer. This section is 20 marks — the largest single block.
- Budget ~25 minutes here. Do one-step questions first (series, percentages, ratio, odd one out, clock angle), then the 2-step ones.
- Never start long algebra: plug the options in (ages, numbers, notes problems) — often faster.
- With −0.25, a guess pays only if you can cut 2 options. If you can eliminate even one, a guess is break-even or better.
- Use 100 as base for % questions; LCM as total work for time & work; × 5/18 for km/h → m/s.
- Revise 1 chapter a day with its MCQs; re-do wrong ones after 3 days.

chapters.title: 1. Number System, HCF–LCM & Simplification
chapters.notes:
### 1.1 Types of numbers
| Type | Meaning | Remember |
|---|---|---|
| Natural (N) | 1, 2, 3 … | Smallest natural number = 1 |
| Whole (W) | 0, 1, 2, 3 … | 0 is whole but not natural |
| Integers (Z) | … −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 … | 0 is neither positive nor negative |
| Rational | p/q, q ≠ 0 | All terminating & recurring decimals |
| Irrational | Non-terminating, non-recurring | √2, √3, π |
| Prime | Exactly 2 factors | 25 primes from 1–100; 2 = only even prime |
| Composite | More than 2 factors | 1 is neither prime nor composite |
| Co-prime | HCF = 1 | (8, 15), (16, 27) — need not be prime |

### 1.2 Divisibility rules
| By | Rule | By | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Last digit even | 8 | Last 3 digits ÷ 8 |
| 3 | Digit sum ÷ 3 | 9 | Digit sum ÷ 9 |
| 4 | Last 2 digits ÷ 4 | 10 | Last digit 0 |
| 5 | Last digit 0 or 5 | 11 | (Sum of odd-place digits) − (sum of even-place digits) = 0 or multiple of 11 |
| 6 | Divisible by 2 and 3 | 12 | Divisible by 3 and 4 |

### 1.3 Unit digit (cyclicity)
| Base ends in | Cycle | Length |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2, 4, 8, 6 | 4 |
| 3 | 3, 9, 7, 1 | 4 |

| Base ends in | Cycle | Length |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 7, 9, 3, 1 | 4 |
| 8 | 8, 4, 2, 6 | 4 |
| 4 | 4, 6 (odd power 4, even power 6) | 2 |
| 9 | 9, 1 (odd 9, even 1) | 2 |
| 0, 1, 5, 6 | Same digit always | 1 |

- ⚡ Shortcut: Divide the power by 4. Remainder r → use the r-th term of the cycle. Remainder 0 → use the 4th term.
- Example: Unit digit of 7⁹⁵?
- 95 ÷ 4 leaves 3 → 3rd term of (7, 9, 3, 1) = 3.
### 1.4 HCF & LCM
- HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers (only for two numbers).
- HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators. LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators.
- Greatest number dividing a, b, c leaving remainders r₁, r₂, r₃ = HCF(a−r₁, b−r₂, c−r₃).
- Greatest number dividing a, b, c leaving the same remainder = HCF of the differences (b−a, c−b, c−a).
- Least number which, divided by x, y, z, leaves remainder r in each case = LCM(x, y, z) + r.
- Bells / lights ringing together again = LCM of their intervals.
- Example: Greatest number that divides 1657 and 2037 leaving remainders 6 and 5?
- HCF(1651, 2032) = 127.
- Example: Least number which leaves remainder 5 when divided by 12, 15 and 20?
- LCM = 60 → 60 + 5 = 65.
### 1.5 Simplification & speed tricks
- VBODMAS: Vinculum (bar) → Brackets ( ), { }, [ ] → Of → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction. 18 ÷ 3 × 2 + 4 − 6 = 12 + 4 − 6 = 10.
- (a+b)² − (a−b)² = 4ab; (a+b)² + (a−b)² = 2(a²+b²); a² − b² = (a+b)(a−b).
- a³ + b³ = (a+b)(a² − ab + b²); a³ − b³ = (a−b)(a² + ab + b²). If a+b+c = 0 then a³+b³+c³ = 3abc.
- Square of a number ending in 5: 65² → 6×7 = 42, write 25 → 4225.
- (n+k)(n−k) = n² − k². e.g. 8798 × 8792 = 8795² − 9, so add 9 to get a perfect square (WBCS 2023).
- Recurring decimal: 0.ab = ab/99; 0.ab = (ab − a)/90.
- Number of factors of N = pᵃ·qᵇ·rᶜ is (a+1)(b+1)(c+1). 360 = 2³·3²·5 → 4×3×2 = 24.
- Sum 1 to n = n(n+1)/2; squares = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6; cubes = [n(n+1)/2]²; first n odd numbers = n².
- Counting digits: 7 appears 19 times when writing 10 to 100 (9 times in units place + 10 times in 70–79).

- ১ মৌলিক বা যৌগিক কোনোটিই নয়; ২ একমাত্র জোড় মৌলিক সংখ্যা; ১–১০০-র মধ্যে ২৫টি মৌলিক সংখ্যা।

chapters.title: 2. Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount
chapters.notes:
### 2.1 Fraction ↔ percentage (learn by heart)
| Fraction | % | Fraction | % | Fraction | % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1/2 | 50 | 1/7 | 14.28 | 1/12 | 8.33 |
| 1/3 | 33.33 | 1/8 | 12.5 | 1/15 | 6.67 |
| 1/4 | 25 | 1/9 | 11.11 | 1/16 | 6.25 |
| 1/5 | 20 | 1/10 | 10 | 1/20 | 5 |
| 1/6 | 16.67 | 1/11 | 9.09 | 1/25 | 4 |

### 2.2 Percentage formulas
- Successive change of a% and b%: net = a + b + ab/100 (use − sign for decrease). +10% then −10% = −1%.
- Length −20%, breadth +20% → area −20 + 20 − 4 = −4% (WBCS 2024).
- Price up r% → cut consumption by r/(100+r) × 100% to keep spending same. Price down r% → consumption can rise by r/(100−r) × 100%.
- A is r% more than B → B is r/(100+r) × 100% less than A. (25% more ⇒ 20% less.)
- Population / depreciation: P(1 ± r/100)ⁿ.
- x% of y = y% of x (8% of 50 = 50% of 8 = 4).
- Exam pass/fail: if a% fail in X, b% in Y, c% in both → pass in both = 100 − (a + b − c).
- Marks problem: two candidates' marks differ by d% of total = (fail margin + extra marks).
### 2.3 Profit, loss & discount
| Item | Formula |
|---|---|
| Profit % | (SP − CP)/CP × 100 (always on CP) |
| SP | CP × (100 + P%)/100 or CP × (100 − L%)/100 |
| Discount % | (MP − SP)/MP × 100 (always on Marked Price) |
| Mark-up m%, discount d% | Net profit % = m − d − md/100 |
| Item | Formula |
| Successive discounts a%, b% | Single discount = a + b − ab/100 |
| CP of x items = SP of y items | Profit % = (x − y)/y × 100 |
| False weight (sells at CP) | Gain % = (True − False)/False × 100 |
| Cheats x% while buying and x% while selling | (1 + x/100)² − 1 → 20% each way gives 44% |
| Two items same SP, x% gain & x% loss | Always loss of x²/100 % |

- Example: Sugar price rises 25%. By how much must a family cut consumption?
- 25/125 × 100 = 20%.
- Example: Marked 40% above CP, discount 20%. Profit?
- 40 − 20 − (40×20)/100 = 12%.
- Example: Shopkeeper uses 900 g for 1 kg and sells at CP.
- 100/900 × 100 = 11.11% gain.
- Example: Sold at 10% loss; ₹40 more would give 10% gain. CP? (WBCS 2013)
- 20% of CP = 40 ⇒ CP = ₹200.
- ⚡ Shortcut: Use 100 as the base. For “profit doubles/triples” type questions, write SP = CP + P and form one equation.
## বাংলা নোট — অধ্যায় ২
- পরপর a% ও b% পরিবর্তন হলে মোট পরিবর্তন = a + b + ab/100 (কমলে মাইনাস চিহ্ন)।
- দাম r% বাড়লে খরচ একই রাখতে ব্যবহার কমাতে হবে r/(100+r) × 100%।
- লাভ-ক্ষতি সবসময় ক্রয়মূল্যের (CP) উপর; ছাড় সবসময় ধার্যমূল্যের (MP) উপর।
- একই বিক্রয়মূল্যে একটিতে x% লাভ ও অন্যটিতে x% ক্ষতি হলে মোট x²/100 % ক্ষতি।
- ভুল ওজন: লাভ% = (আসল − ভুল) ÷ ভুল × 100। ক্রয় ও বিক্রয় দুই ক্ষেত্রেই ২০% ঠকালে লাভ ৪৪%।
- x টি জিনিসের ক্রয়মূল্য = y টির বিক্রয়মূল্য হলে লাভ% = (x − y)/y × 100।

chapters.title: 3. Ratio, Partnership, Ages, Average & Mixtures
chapters.notes:
### 3.1 Ratio & proportion
- A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5 → make B equal: 8 : 12 : 15.
- Ratio of fractions ½ : ⅓ : ¼ → multiply by LCM 12 → 6 : 4 : 3.
- Mean proportional of a, b = √(ab). Third proportional = b²/a. Fourth proportional of a, b, c = bc/a.
- Dividing ₹N in a : b : c → A gets N × a/(a+b+c).
- Sides in ratio and perimeter given: one part = perimeter ÷ sum of ratio terms (WBCS 2023: 1/20 :
- 1/15 : 1/12 = 3:4:5, perimeter 30 → longest 12.5 cm).
- Shadow/height questions are simple proportion: 64 ft building, 96 ft shadow; 180 ft shadow → 120 ft tower.
### 3.2 Partnership
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time. A puts ₹50,000 for 12 months, B ₹60,000 for 8 months → 6,00,000 : 4,80,000 = 5 : 4. A working partner first takes salary, rest is shared.
### 3.3 Ages
- Take present ages as ratio units (3x, 4x); add/subtract years to both; solve one equation.
- Shortcut: check the options — present ages must satisfy both conditions.
- Age difference between two people never changes.
- Example: Ages are 3:4 now; after 5 years 4:5. Present ages?
- (3x+5)/(4x+5) = 4/5 ⇒ x = 5 → 15 and 20.
### 3.4 Average
- Average = sum ÷ number. Average of consecutive numbers = middle term (or average of first and last).
- New person joins and average rises by k: his value = old average + k × (new count).
- Average speed for equal distances = 2xy/(x + y). Half distance at 20 m/s, half at 30 m/s → 24 m/s (WBCS 2024).
- Average of 6 consecutive odd numbers is 64 → numbers 59 … 69, largest 69 (WBCS 2022).
- Weighted average: boys avg 52, girls 42, class 50 → boys : girls = (50−42) : (52−50) = 4 : 1 → boys 80% (WBCS 2024).
### 3.5 Mixture & alligation
| Cheaper (c) | Dearer (d) |
|---|---|

- Mean (m)
| (d − m) Cheaper : Dearer = (d − m) : (m − c) | (m − c) |
|---|---|

- Rice ₹40 and ₹55 mixed to sell at ₹50 → (55−50) : (50−40) = 1 : 2.
- Replacement: from V litres of pure liquid, x litres taken out and replaced n times → pure left = V(1 − x/V)ⁿ.
- Two mixtures A:B = 2:3 and 5:4 mixed so that A = B → use alligation on the fraction of A: 2/5 and 5/9 around ½ → ratio 5 : 9 (WBCS 2018).
## বাংলা নোট — অধ্যায় ৩
- A:B ও B:C দেওয়া থাকলে B-কে সমান করে A:B:C বানাও। ভগ্নাংশের অনুপাতকে হরগুলির ল.সা.গু দিয়ে গুণ করো।
- মধ্য সমানুপাতী = √(ab); চতুর্থ সমানুপাতী = bc/a।
- অংশীদারিতে লাভ ভাগ হয় মূলধন × সময় অনুপাতে।

chapters.title: 4. Simple & Compound Interest
chapters.notes:
### 4.1 Simple interest (SI)
- SI = P × R × T / 100; Amount A = P + SI.
- Sum doubles in T years → R = 100/T. Becomes n times in T years → R = 100(n − 1)/T.
- If SI = P/k and R = T, then R² = 100/k.
- Amount A₁ after T₁ years and A₂ after T₂ years → SI per year = (A₂ − A₁)/(T₂ − T₁); P = A₁ − T₁ × yearly SI.
### 4.2 Compound interest (CI)
- A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, CI = A − P.
- Half-yearly: rate R/2, time 2n. Quarterly: rate R/4, time 4n.
- CI − SI for 2 years = P(R/100)². For 3 years = P(R/100)²(3 + R/100).
- Effective rate for 2 years = 2R + R²/100 (10% → 21%; 5% → 10.25%; 20% → 44%).
- If a sum becomes k times in n years (CI) → k² times in 2n, k³ times in 3n years.
- Rule of 72: money doubles in about 72/R years at CI.
| Rate | 2 years CI on 100 | 3 years CI on 100 |
|---|---|---|
| 5% | 10.25 | 15.7625 |
| 10% | 21 | 33.1 |
| 20% | 44 | 72.8 |

- Example: CI on ₹10,000 at 10% for 2 years?
- 21% of 10,000 = ₹2,100.
- Example: CI − SI on ₹15,000 at 10% for 2 years?
- 15,000 × (1/10)² = ₹150.
- Example: ₹8,000 at 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 1 year?
- 8,000 × 1.05² = 8,820 → CI ₹820.
- Example: ₹3,000 in bank and ₹2,500 in post office for 1 year; bank rate is ½% higher; total interest ₹235. Post-office rate? (WBCS 2017)
- 30(r + ½) + 25r = 235 ⇒ 55r = 220 ⇒ r = 4%.
## বাংলা নোট — অধ্যায় ৪
- সরল সুদ = আসল × হার × সময় ÷ ১০০। T বছরে দ্বিগুণ হলে হার = 100/T।
- চক্রবৃদ্ধি: সমূল = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ; ষাণ্মাসিক হলে হার অর্ধেক, সময় দ্বিগুণ।
- ২ বছরে চক্রবৃদ্ধি সুদ − সরল সুদ = P(R/100)²।
- ২ বছরের কার্যকর হার = 2R + R²/100 (১০% → ২১%)।
- চক্রবৃদ্ধিতে n বছরে k গুণ হলে 2n বছরে k² গুণ।
- ৭২-এর নিয়ম: R% হারে টাকা প্রায় 72/R বছরে দ্বিগুণ হয়।

chapters.title: 5. Time & Work, Pipes, Time–Speed–Distance, Trains & Boats
chapters.notes:
### 5.1 Time & work — LCM method
- Take total work = LCM of the days. Each person's efficiency = total ÷ own days.
- A in a days, B in b days → together ab/(a + b) days.
- A is k times as efficient as B → A takes 1/k of B's time.
- M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂ (men × days × hours ÷ work).
- Pipes: filling pipe = +efficiency, outlet / leak = −efficiency. Same LCM method.
- Example: A does a job in 12 days, B in 18. Together?
- Work 36; A 3/day, B 2/day → 36/5 = 7.2 days.
- Example: Pipe A fills in 10 h, B empties in 15 h. Both open?
- Tank 30; 3 − 2 = 1/h → 30 h.
### 5.2 Speed, time, distance
- km/h × 5/18 = m/s; m/s × 18/5 = km/h. (72 km/h = 20 m/s, 54 = 15, 36 = 10, 90 = 25.)
- Same distance: speed ratio a : b → time ratio b : a.
- Late / early: distance = (S₁ × S₂)/(S₂ − S₁) × time difference.
- Relative speed: same direction → subtract; opposite → add.
- Ant at 75 cm/s for a day = 75 × 86,400 cm = 64,800 m (WBCS 2020) — watch the units!
- Climbing pole: +5 day, −4 night, 75 ft pole → net +1/day till the last day: (75 − 5) + 1 = 71st day (WBCS 2020).
### 5.3 Trains
| Train crosses … | Distance covered |
|---|---|
| a pole / man / signal | Length of train |
| a platform / bridge / tunnel | Train + platform |
| another train (opposite) | L₁ + L₂ at speed S₁ + S₂ |

| Train crosses … | Distance covered |
|---|---|
| another train (same direction) | L₁ + L₂ at speed S₁ − S₂ |

- Example: Train 60 km/h crosses a 1.5 km tunnel in 2 min. Length? (WBCS 2024)
- 60 km/h = 1 km/min → 2 km in 2 min → train = 500 m.
- Example: A man on a 120 m platform sees a train pass him in 5 s and the platform in 15 s.
- Length? (WBCS 2017)
- L/5 = (L+120)/15 ⇒ L = 60 m.
### 5.4 Boats & streams
- Downstream D = u + v; upstream U = u − v (u = boat in still water, v = stream).
- u = (D + U)/2; v = (D − U)/2.
## বাংলা নোট — অধ্যায় ৫
- সময় ও কাজ: দিনগুলির ল.সা.গু = মোট কাজ; প্রতিদিনের কাজ = মোট ÷ নিজের দিন।
- A a দিনে, B b দিনে করলে একসঙ্গে ab/(a+b) দিন। ফুটো/নির্গম নলের কাজ বিয়োগ হবে।
- কিমি/ঘণ্টাকে মি/সেকেন্ডে নিতে × 5/18।
- ট্রেন খুঁটি পেরোলে দূরত্ব = ট্রেনের দৈর্ঘ্য; প্ল্যাটফর্ম পেরোলে = ট্রেন + প্ল্যাটফর্ম।

chapters.notes:
### 7.1 Number series — check in this order
| Step | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Differences (1st, then 2nd level) | 6, 11, 21, 36, 56 → diff 5, 10, 15, 20 → next 81 |
| 2 | Ratio / × ± k | 4, 10, 22, 46 → ×2 + 2 → 94; 3, 7, 15, 31 → ×2 + 1 |
| 3 | Squares / cubes ± k | 2, 5, 10, 17, 26 → n² + 1; 0, 7, 26, 63 → n³ − 1 |
| 4 | Differences are squares / cubes | 1, 2, 10, 37, 101 → +1, +8, +27, +64 → +125 = 226 |
| 5 | Alternate (two series mixed) | 3, 8, 6, 14, 9, 20 → (3, 6, 9) and (8, 14, 20) |
| 6 | Fibonacci-type (sum of previous two) | 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29 → 47 |
| 7 | Primes | 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 → 23 |
| 8 | n(n+1), n² − n | 2, 6, 12, 20, 30 → 42 |

- ⚡ Shortcut: If the series grows slowly → think differences. Grows fast → think × or powers. Goes up & down → alternate series.
### 7.2 Letter series
- Position numbers: A1 … Z26. Learn EJOTY = 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 to find any letter fast.
- Reverse position = 27 − position (A↔Z, B↔Y …). Opposite pairs: AZ, BY, CX, DW, EV, FU, GT, HS, IR, JQ, KP, LO, MN.
- A, C, F, J, O, ? → gaps +2, +3, +4, +5, +6 → U.
### 7.3 Analogy
| Type | Example |
|---|---|
| Worker : place / tool | Doctor : Hospital; Carpenter : Saw |
| Instrument : what it measures | Thermometer : Temperature; Barometer : Pressure; Seismograph : Earthquake |
| Product : raw material | Paper : Pulp; Cloth : Yarn |
| Type | Example |
| Young one | Cow : Calf; Dog : Puppy; Horse : Foal |
| Number | 9 : 81 (square); 4 : 64 (cube); letters ACE : BDF (+1 each) |

### 7.4 Classification (odd one out)
- Numbers: prime vs composite, even vs odd, perfect squares/cubes, divisible by a common number.
- Words: alloy vs metal (Brass, Bronze, Steel are alloys), synonym groups, category (fruits, tools).
- Letters: equal gaps (BDF, MOQ, RTV are +2 +2) vs unequal gaps (GIL).

- k-th letter from the right = (27 − k)-th from the left.

### 8.2 Types of coding
| Type | How to crack | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Letter shift | Write positions, find +/− pattern | MANGO → NBOHP (+1) |
| Increasing shift | +1, +2, +3 … or +2, +3, +4 … | FRIEND → HUMJTK (+2 … +7) |
| Opposite letters | Pair with 27 − position | CAT → XZG |
| Reverse | Read backward | TRAIN → NIART |
| Letter → digit | Make a letter-digit table from given words | ROSE 6821, CHAIR 73456 → S=2, E=1 … |
| Sum of positions | Add letter values | CAT = 3 + 1 + 20 = 24 |
| Sentence coding | Common words ↔ common codes | See example |
| Substitution | Follow the renamed word exactly | If water is called ‘air’, we drink ‘air’ |

- Example: ‘pit dar na’ = you are good; ‘dar tok pa’ = good and bad; ‘tim na tok’ = they are bad.

chapters.title: 9. Directions, Blood Relations & Ranking
chapters.notes:
### 9.1 Directions
**N**
| NW W← ✦ →E SW | ↑ ↓ S | NE SE |
|---|---|---|

- Right turn = clockwise 90°; left turn = anticlockwise 90°. Facing North: right → East, left → West.
- Draw every move on paper; shortest distance by Pythagoras (3-4-5, 6-8-10, 5-12-13).
- Shadow: sunrise (morning) sun in East → shadow falls West; evening → shadow falls East. No shadow at noon.
- Rotated directions: if SE becomes N (3 steps of 45° anticlockwise), rotate every direction the same way.
- Example: Walks 10 m North, turns right 6 m, turns right 18 m. Distance from start?
- Ends 6 m East and 8 m South → √(36+64) = 10 m, South-East.
### 9.2 Blood relations
| Phrase | Means |
|---|---|
| Father's / mother's father | Grandfather (paternal / maternal) |
| Father's brother | Uncle (paternal) — কাকা/জেঠা |
| Mother's brother | Maternal uncle — মামা |
| Brother's / sister's son | Nephew — ভাইপো / ভাগ্নে |
| Brother's / sister's daughter | Niece — ভাইঝি / ভাগ্নী |
| Uncle's / aunt's child | Cousin |
| Husband's / wife's brother | Brother-in-law |
| Son's wife | Daughter-in-law |

- Start from the end of the sentence (“…of my mother”) and work backward.
- “My father's only son” = me (if male). “My mother's only daughter” = me (if female).
- Draw a family tree: + male, − female, = couple, vertical line = next generation.
- Coded relations (P + Q = P is husband of Q): translate each symbol one by one; don't assume gender.
### 9.3 Ranking & order
- Total = (rank from left) + (rank from right) − 1. Same for top/bottom.
- Interchange: when two people swap, use the new position of one with the old position of the other.
- Add failed / absent students to the total of those ranked.

chapters.title: 10. Syllogism, Venn Diagrams & Statement–Conclusion
chapters.notes:
### 10.1 Syllogism — conversion & rules
| Statement | Converts to | Note |
|---|---|---|
| All A are B | Some B are A | “All B are A” does NOT follow |
| Some A are B | Some B are A |  |
| No A is B | No B is A | Also: Some A are not B |
| Some A are not B | No conversion |  |
| 1st premise + 2nd premise |  | Conclusion (A–C) |
| All + All |  | All |
| All + No |  | No |
| Some + All |  | Some |
| Some + No |  | Some not (Some A are not C) |
| No + All |  | Some C are not A (reverse) |
| All + Some, Some + Some, No + No |  | No definite conclusion |

- Draw the minimum (simplest) Venn diagram; a conclusion follows only if it is true in every possible diagram.
- Either–or: when two conclusions are a complementary pair (Some A are B / No A is B) with the same subject and neither follows on its own.
### 10.2 Venn diagrams
| Relationship | Picture | Example |
|---|---|---|
| One inside another inside another | Concentric circles | Kolkata ⊂ West Bengal ⊂ India |
| Two separate inside one | Two small circles in a big circle | Animals ⊃ Cows, Dogs |
| All three separate | Three separate circles | Pen, Table, River |
| Relationship | Picture | Example |
| One inside another, third overlaps both | Mothers ⊂ Women; Doctors overlap both | Doctors, Women, Mothers |

Counting: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B). Neither = Total − n(A ∪ B).
### 10.3 Statement – assumption / conclusion
- Assumption = what the speaker takes for granted (unstated). Advertisements assume people want the result and respond to ads.
- Conclusion must follow directly from the statement only — no outside knowledge.
- Words like ‘only’, ‘always’, ‘all’, ‘never’ in options usually make them wrong.
## বাংলা নোট — অধ্যায় ১০
- সব A হল B → কিছু B হল A (কিন্তু সব B হল A নয়)।
- সব + সব = সব; সব + কোনো নয় = কোনো নয়; কিছু + সব = কিছু; কিছু + কোনো নয় = কিছু নয়।
- সব সম্ভাব্য চিত্রে সত্য হলেই সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণযোগ্য। পরিপূরক জোড়া হলে ‘হয় I নয় II’।
- ভেন গণনা: n(A∪B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A∩B)।
- বিবৃতি-সিদ্ধান্তে বাইরের জ্ঞান ব্যবহার করবে না; ‘শুধু’, ‘সবসময়’ জাতীয় শব্দ সাধারণত ভুল বিকল্পে থাকে।

chapters.title: 11. Clock, Calendar, Symbols, Dice & Seating
chapters.notes:
### 11.1 Clock
- Angle between hands = |30H − 5.5M| (if > 180°, subtract from 360°).
- Minute hand gains 55 minute-spaces per hour over the hour hand.
- In 12 h: hands coincide 11 times, are opposite 11 times, at right angles 22 times. In a day: 22, 22, 44.
- Hands coincide between H and H+1 at 60H/11 minutes past H.
- Mirror image: 11:60 − given time (e.g. 3:15 → 8:45). Water image: 18:30 − time.
- Bell striking the hour (1 at 1 o'clock … 12 at 12): 78 strokes in 12 h, 156 in a day (WBCS 2018:
- 312 in 2 days).
- Example: Angle at 3:40?
- |90 − 220| = 130°.
### 11.2 Calendar
- Odd days: ordinary year = 1, leap year = 2. 100 years = 5, 200 = 3, 300 = 1, 400 = 0 odd days.
- Leap year: divisible by 4; a century year only if divisible by 400 (2000 yes, 1900 & 2100 no).
- Same date next year moves by 1 day (2 days if Feb 29 falls in between).
- Calendar of an ordinary year repeats after 6 or 11 years (2026 → 2037); a leap year after 28 years.
- Day codes: Sun 0, Mon 1, … Sat 6. Month odd days: Jan 3, Feb 0/1, Mar 3, Apr 2, May 3, Jun 2, Jul 3, Aug 3, Sep 2, Oct 3, Nov 2, Dec 3.
- Anchors: 15 Aug 1947 = Friday; 1 Jan 2026 = Thursday; 9 Nov 2026 = Monday.
### 11.3 Mathematical operations & symbols
Replace each sign as told, then apply BODMAS. Write the new expression fully before calculating.
### 11.4 Dice
- On a standard die opposite faces add up to 7 (1–6, 2–5, 3–4).
- From two positions: the common face's neighbours tell you the opposite pairs; numbers seen adjacent to a face can never be opposite it.
### 11.5 Seating arrangement
- Linear, facing North: your right = viewer's right. Facing South: reverse.
- Circular, facing centre: right = anticlockwise, left = clockwise.
- Fix the definite clues first (ends, middle, opposite), then fill relative clues.
## বাংলা নোট — অধ্যায় ১১
- ঘড়ির কাঁটার কোণ = |30H − 5.5M|। দিনে কাঁটা ২২ বার মেলে, ৪৪ বার সমকোণ হয়।

- সাধারণ বছরে ১ বিজোড় দিন, অধিবর্ষে ২। শতবর্ষ অধিবর্ষ হবে শুধু ৪০০ দিয়ে বিভাজ্য হলে।

- Revise old papers — repeats are common.
### 12.2 Counting shortcuts
| Situation | Formula | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Handshakes / matches (each pair once) | n(n − 1)/2 | 6 players → 15 matches |
| Captain + vice-captain | n(n − 1) | 11 players → 110 |
| Diagonals of an n-sided polygon | n(n − 3)/2 | Hexagon → 9 |

| Situation | Formula | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Lines through n points (no 3 collinear) | n(n − 1)/2 | 10 points → 45 |

### 12.3 Equation-type puzzles
- Notes / coins: let one count be x, the other (total − x). ₹6000 in 48 notes of ₹200 & ₹100 → 100x = 6000 − 4800 → x = 12.
- Marks with negative: +a right, −b wrong, all attempted: right = (score + b × total)/(a + b).
- Custom operator a * b: just substitute values carefully.
- Periodic events (trains every 45 min): work backward from the next event.
